system_prompt_style.note: No harness code released; only Lean solutions.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: LEAP first attempts direct formalization with compiler-feedback revision and LeanSearch(Gao et al., 2024) retrieval.
env_context_strategy.note: LeanSearch retrieval mechanism (lexical vs embedding) not stated; the state reader also retrieves related lemmas from the DAG. Closest value chosen.

observation_format.evidence_quote: iteratively correcting errors via compiler feedback.
observation_format.note: The observation format is inferred from the Lean compiler feedback.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: LEAP then first attempts adirect proofby generating an informal proof, translating it into Lean code, and checking the candidate with the Lean compiler.
edit_primitive.note: Inferred that candidate proofs are regenerated whole; the revision format is not stated.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: it identifies unpromising decompositions, triggers backtracking, and encourages exploration of alternative strategies. Currently, LEAP uses a simple DFS over the DAG with backtracking.
loop_primitives.note: generate_test_repair: the Lean compiler feedback revision loop, with up to 20 steps (Sec. 5.1). fixed_pipeline: the stage sequence prover->verifier->reviser.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: LEAP incrementally drafts blueprints, decomposes Lean goals into supporting lemmas, and maintains the evolving proof plan as an AND-OR DAG.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: an LLM reviewer assesses the quality of the decomposition
multi_agent_topology.note: A single agent with role-specific LLM calls (prover, reviser, reviewer). Per the rules, a reviewer model is still coded as single.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The agent then recursively processes the newly created subgoals.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: This successful reproduction demonstrates LEAP’s capability to reliably translate complex, existing literature into high-assurance formal proofs without human intervention.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: OR nodes represent open goals or lemma statements, each of which may be resolved by any valid proof strategy, while AND nodes represent candidate decompositions

long_term_memory.note: The DAG memory is within a run; persistence across runs is not stated.

self_verification.evidence_quote: LEAP uses verification at two levels. First, the Lean compiler formally checks candidate proofs and sketches

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Evaluation settings:⋄ indicates pass@128, while† indicates rollout=2.
retry_policy.note: Rollouts were used in evaluation. Revision is capped at 20 compiler-feedback steps (Sec. 5.1).

termination_condition.evidence_quote: causing the agent to repeat the same unproductive decomposition until its search budget is exhausted.
termination_condition.note: The run ends when Lean verifies the root (PROVED) or the budget is exhausted; the budget type is not specified.

timeouts.note: The 7-day limit applied to the Hilbert baseline, not to LEAP.

eval_hooks.note: The repo ships benchmark CSVs and solutions but no runner.

guardrails.evidence_quote: The verified sketch is then passed to thestate writer, which checks that the update preserves acyclicity before committing it to the DAG.

target_domain.evidence_quote: an agentic framework that enables general-purpose foundation models to achieve state-of-the-art performance on automated formal theorem proving.

open_source.evidence_quote: The Lean solutions generated by LEAP are available at
open_source.note: The repo is Apache 2.0, but only the outputs are released; no harness code is in the file tree.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: an agentic framework usingonlygeneral LLMs for formal math.
model_agnostic.note: Evaluated only with Gemini-3.1-pro; no abstraction layer is shown.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: LEAP: Supercharging LLMs for Formal Mathematics with Agentic Frameworks
